paragraphs: MoonshotAI Kimi is a family of large language models from the developer Moonshot AI, offered through the Kimi API Platform. The platform provides Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, Kimi K2.6 and other large language model APIs, supporting long context, multimodal understanding, and Tool Calling. Moonshot AI says Kimi K3 is its flagship model for long-horizon coding and end-to-end knowledge work, with a 1M-token context window and industry-leading intelligence. Kimi K2.7 Code is for coding, multimodal input, thinking, tool calling, and 256K-token contexts, and has a high-speed variant. Kimi K2.6 covers text, image, and video understanding, thinking mode, tool calling, and a 256K-token context window.

The family also includes thinking modes, with reasoning effort values low, high, and max to balance Kimi K3 reasoning depth, latency, and token usage. Moonshot AI offers the models through the Kimi API Platform, which is pay-as-you-go with no subscription plan, and through Kimi Code, a separate coding product whose API keys are not interchangeable with Open Platform keys. Kimi Code CLI is a terminal-based AI agent that can use an API Key created on Kimi API Platform. The platform also documents integrations such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, and ModelScope MCP Server.

price_limits.summary: Across the 7 versions, input prices run from $0.43 to $0.8 per million tokens and output prices from $2.3 to $15. Kimi K2 0711 is the cheapest, at $0.57 per million input tokens and $2.3 per million output tokens. Kimi K3 has the largest context window, 1,048,576 tokens.

family_reading.text: MoonshotAI Kimi is an open weights family, with all 7 versions publishing weights, and 5 of the 7 supporting reasoning. Context windows run from 131072 to 1048576 tokens, and the line accepts image, text and video input while returning text only. The newest version, Kimi K3, offers the largest context at 1048576 tokens and the longest output at 943718 tokens, priced at $0.72 per million input and $13 output. Other versions sit near $0.45 to $0.95 input and $2.25 to $4 output, so K3 is the costly option. The facts suggest the family suits long document, image and video understanding with reasoning, and self hosting given open weights. Limits are the text only output, the higher cost of the largest context version, and the fact that two earlier versions lack reasoning support.
